notes: Most restaurants and shops on the island take cards, but carrying cash TL makes things easier at the Wednesday market, at wineries and in small tradesmen's restaurants.
Bozcaada is very small: almost everywhere is a 10-25 minute walk from the centre. Dolmuş (minibus) services are limited, and a bike is the most practical way to get around.
Leaving a tip of around 10% on top of the bill is common in meyhanes and restaurants; if the waiter adds service themselves, don't add it again.
July and August are high season: book boat tours, vineyard tours and meyhane tables at least 2-3 days ahead, or you may not find a place.
The sun is very strong between 12:00 and 16:00; stay on the beach or in the shade at these hours, and sunscreen and a hat are essential.
The island is very safe and night walks are easy, but there are no lifeguards in bays without facilities such as Habbele and Sulubahçe, so swim carefully.
When visiting wineries, don't enter the vines without permission or pick grapes; ask permission before photographing a local's home.

niche.name: Maya Bozcaada
niche.why_hidden: It is set in a garden hidden among pines and vineyards on the island; there is no sign, and it rarely appears on social media. Selçuk Bey does not host anyone without an appointment. This table brings together sourdough bread and the island's goat cheese, and most mainstream guides skip it.
niche.access_instructions: Book by phone or WhatsApp at least 1-2 days before your visit; without an appointment you won't get a table. Amerikan Çeşme is a 10-minute taxi ride from the centre. There are no signs along the vineyard roads, so confirm the address before you go.
niche.season: Open from April to October; it may be closed in the winter months, so confirm when booking.
niche.insider_tip: Ask about the set menu in advance; on some days the menu includes meat brought from Istanbul. Ask for the sourdough bread with goat cheese. Lunchtime is quieter than the evening.
niche.show_reason: Rezervasyonsuz bulunamayan, sadece adayı iyi bilenlerin gittiği bir sofra; sourdough ekmek kültürü ile organik keçi peynirini bir araya getiren nadir bir deneyim sunuyor.
niche.address: Cumhuriyet Mahallesi, Amerikan Çeşme Mevkii, Küme Evleri No:31, Bozcaada, Çanakkale 17680

days.theme: Bozcaada's signatures: fortress, Greek quarter and Ayazma

stops.name: Bozcaada Castle
stops.tips: It opens at 09:00 in summer, and the first hours are the quietest. Look at the amphorae and island history in the small museum inside, then climb to the upper level for views of the Aegean from the walls.

stops.name: Cumhuriyet Mahallesi (Greek Quarter) Walk
stops.tips: Photograph the Greek houses with cellars and the colourful doors along the stone streets that cross at right angles; the best light is before noon. To escape the crowds, turn into the back streets instead of the main bazaar.

stops.name: Hafızın Yeri
stops.tips: A traditional tradesmen's restaurant with daily dishes, and a place locals come to as well. Ask for one of the olive oil dishes and the seasonal salad; service is quick at lunchtime.

stops.name: Ayazma Beach
stops.tips: The island's most famous and widest beach, with fine sand and cool water; sunbeds and umbrellas are included in the price. In summer a dolmuş (minibus) runs from the centre, otherwise it is a 10-minute taxi ride.

stops.name: Dört Hanımeli Restaurant
stops.tips: Home cooking made by island women; be sure to try the island mantı (small dumplings) and stuffed courgette flowers. It is small and friendly, and booking is recommended for the evening.

backups.name: 19 Oda Kahvaltı & Cafe
backups.tips: An alternative if Hafızın Yeri is full: it serves simple but filling homemade plates. It is close to the centre, and there may be a short wait at lunchtime.

backups.name: Namazgah Fountain
backups.tips: An easy-to-spot historic fountain on the Greek Quarter route, and a good stop for a photo break. Free and always open.

days.theme: The west end: windmills, lighthouse and hidden coves

stops.name: Bozcaada Windmills
stops.tips: From the large car park behind the Greek Quarter, take the lavender-scented stone path and walk for 15-20 minutes. Early in the morning the light and wind are ideal for photos.

stops.name: Bike Tour of the Vineyard Roads
stops.tips: Hire a bike from the rental points in the centre and ride from the windmills towards the vineyard roads; the road is flat with little car traffic. The daily rental fee is per person, and you can also agree a half-day rate.
A simple tradesmen's stop where locals go for köfte sandwiches and ıslak burger (soft, sauce-soaked burger). Quick and filling, and perfectly timed after the bike tour.

stops.name: Habbele Bay
stops.tips: A pebbly bay with no facilities, surrounded by pine trees; the water does not suddenly get deep. Bring your own water and umbrella, ideal for an afternoon away from the crowds.

stops.name: Polente Lighthouse
stops.tips: Bozcaada's best-known sunset spot; arrive 40 minutes before sunset and try framing the lighthouse with the wind turbines. It is about a 20-minute walk from the centre, or 10 minutes by car.

stops.name: Şükrü Usta Zeytinyağlı Ev Yemekleri
stops.tips: One of the island's classics for home-style olive oil dishes; the artichokes and fresh green beans are excellent in season. A quiet, family-run table.

backups.name: 49 Polente Cafe Bar
backups.tips: A handy option for a drink while watching the sunset in front of the lighthouse. There is seating on the street, and the atmosphere is lively.

backups.name: Sulubahçe Beach
backups.tips: A calm bay with no facilities between Habbele and Ayazma, good for sunbathing on the rocks. Campers like it too, and there is little shade.

days.theme: The soul of Bozcaada: vineyards, wine and a hidden garden

stops.name: Corvus Wine Shop
stops.tips: At the shop in Çınarlı Çarşı, discover the island's best-known modern winery with a short tasting. It is not crowded early in the morning, and the tasting fee depends on the wine you choose.

stops.name: Maya Bozcaada
stops.tips: A table hidden among pines and vineyards in the Amerikan Çeşme area, impossible to get into without an appointment. Ask for the sourdough bread and the island's goat cheese together, and check the set menu in advance.

stops.name: Bozcaada Vineyard and Wine Tasting Tour
stops.tips: You visit different wineries such as Talay and Amadeus and taste at each stop, so you see different producers from this morning's Corvus. In high season, booking at least 2 days ahead is essential.

stops.name: Çamlıbağ Sunset Tractor Tour
stops.tips: Çamlıbağ, the island's first Turkish wine producer, takes you by tractor to its vineyards on summer evenings to watch the sunset with cheese and wine. Confirm the meeting point and time by phone beforehand.

stops.name: Simyon Traditional Meyhane
stops.tips: A classic meyhane (tavern) for experiencing island meze and rakı culture in its authentic form. Share the shrimp güveç (clay-pot casserole) and seasonal mezes; booking is recommended at weekends.

backups.name: Amadeus Wines Tasting Room
backups.tips: A modern tasting room you can visit on its own if the vineyard tour is full. They offer a short tasting set, and you only need to make an appointment.

backups.name: Talay Vineyards Tour
backups.tips: One of the island's long-established producers; if the vineyard tour is cancelled, you can see generations-old traditional production here. Calling the day before is enough for tours.

days.theme: From the sea: hidden coves boat tour

stops.name: Bozcaada Boat Tour
stops.tips: It leaves from the pier with swimming stops at Akvaryum Bay, Mavra (Rabbit) Island and Poyraz Harbour; lunch is included in the tour price. The tour can sell out in high season, so book at least 2 days ahead.

stops.name: Kahve Arası Bozcaada
stops.tips: A calm coffee break to regroup after getting off the boat; try the cold brews. It is within walking distance of the centre, with roomy seating.

stops.name: Kapı 14
stops.tips: Strong on both fish and meze; if it is bluefish (çinekop) or bonito (palamut) season, be sure to ask. It fills up quickly in the evenings, so booking is recommended.

stops.name: Iskele Square
stops.tips: Take an evening stroll on the main ferry square and stop at the ice cream shops; the harbour is lovely for photos with its night lights. Free, with plenty of places to sit.

backups.name: Sapa Restaurant
backups.tips: In a quiet spot, it offers a seasonal cocktail menu and island wines. A good alternative if Kapı 14 is full, with seating by the sea.

backups.name: Poyraz Harbour Viewpoint
backups.tips: If the boat tour is cancelled, this is a bay view reachable by land; you drive along a dirt road. Good for swimming, but there are no facilities.

stops.name: Alaybey Mahallesi Walk
stops.tips: In this part, known as the Turkish Quarter, winding streets and wooden bay-windowed houses stand out. Walk it in comparison with Cumhuriyet Mahallesi to see the architectural difference; free.

stops.name: Di Mari Bozcaada
stops.tips: A bakery and gastronomy stop making long-fermented sourdough bread and focaccia. Come early in the morning and you will catch it fresh from the oven.

stops.name: Çınaraltı Kahvesi
stops.tips: In the shade of the big plane tree, they serve mastic-flavoured coffee and Turkish coffee brewed in a special cezve. In May, island women sometimes sell stuffed courgette flowers here too, so don't miss them if you spot them.

stops.name: Beylik Bay
stops.tips: One of the bays closest to the centre, a 15-minute walk. On the way you pass the ruins of Ayazma Monastery, and you can stop for a brief look.

stops.name: Bozcaada Fish Market
stops.tips: A small market where island fishermen bring their daily catch; it is lively in the late afternoon as the boats return. Ask permission for photos, and ask the price if you want to buy fresh fish.

stops.name: Güveç Restaurant
stops.tips: An affordable address serving home cooking and grill dishes in its small garden. Ask about the day's güveç (clay-pot casserole) and order accordingly.

backups.name: Rengigül Konukevi Breakfast House
backups.tips: If Di Mari is full, this is a rich breakfast alternative with homemade jam and olives in the garden. You sit in a quiet courtyard, and booking is recommended.

backups.name: Alaybey Mosque
backups.tips: A short stop on the Turkish Quarter tour; its exterior architecture completes the character of the neighbourhood. Free, and open to visit outside prayer times.

days.theme: Beyond the island: Assos and Behramkale

stops.name: Assos Ancient City and Temple of Athena
stops.tips: You leave the island on the Yükyeri-Geyikli ferry and reach Behramkale after a drive of about 1 hour 10 minutes; the whole journey there takes about 2 hours. From the Doric temple on the acropolis you can see Lesbos, so set aside some time for the view.

stops.name: Behramkale Village Stone Streets
stops.tips: Explore the village on foot with its stone houses and narrow streets, and browse the small shops selling olive oil and handicrafts. Cars are left in the car park at the top of the village.

stops.name: Alterna Köy Mutfağı Sarmaşık Gülleri Restaurant
stops.tips: A simple address serving village-house home cooking; olive oil dishes and seasonal vegetables stand out. It is quiet at lunchtime, and no booking is needed.

stops.name: Kadırga Bay
stops.tips: 2 km from Behramkale, a long, calm beach facing Lesbos. It is 10 minutes from the village by car or taxi; facilities are limited, so bring water and snacks.

stops.name: Palamud Restaurant
stops.tips: On the stone quay of the ancient harbour, it serves seafood with rakı at sunset. To catch the return ferry, set off around 21:00 in the evening, and confirm the last ferry time in advance.

backups.name: Fenerlihan
backups.tips: If Palamud is full, another address in the ancient harbour serving local flavours. Seafood and olive oil mezes stand out.

backups.name: Assos Ancient Harbour
backups.tips: A small, charming harbour where old warehouse buildings have been restored; you can stroll along the stone quay and rest there until it is time to return. It is also a good spot for swimming.

stops.name: Petti Patisserie
stops.tips: For a modern breakfast stop, a croissant and a flat white make a good pair. In the centre, and easy to find a seat early in the morning.

stops.name: Ayazma Monastery Ruins
stops.tips: A quiet Byzantine-era ruin between Ayazma Beach and Beylik Bay; it is never crowded. Free, and a short walk in comfortable shoes is enough.

stops.name: Iğdelik Beach
stops.tips: Quieter than the main beaches, and a good place for one last swim before leaving the island. There may be no sunbeds, so bring your own towel.

backups.name: Oda Cafe Bar
backups.tips: If Petti is full, a calm coffee break with nostalgic music. Close to the centre, with a quiet atmosphere during the day.

backups.name: Çayır Bay
backups.tips: An alternative quiet bay if Iğdelik is full; facilities are few but the sea is clean. You need a vehicle to get there.
